acceptance_criteria: Claim, reclaim, retry, acknowledgement, sent, suppressed, quarantine, test-leak, collapsed, write-failure, and dead-letter transitions use one declared durability contract.
A successful cross-directory move syncs both changed parents after rename, while a same-parent move syncs that parent once.
Destination-sync failure, source-sync failure, rename failure, and interruption after rename produce an explicit ambiguous reconciliation state rather than ordinary success or blind replay.
Remote acknowledgement is not reported durable until its terminal namespace state is committed.
Accepted local delivery cannot become replay-eligible solely because terminal namespace persistence was unproven.
Cross-filesystem fallback proves file contents, destination publication, and source removal in the required order.
Restart reconciliation converges duplicate source and destination names to one authoritative lifecycle record by stable event identity.
Fault-injection tests assert exact rename and directory-sync ordering plus failures at every boundary.
Platform tests cover supported filesystems and explicitly report where durability guarantees are unavailable.
A structural guard inventories every lifecycle mover, including embedded remote scripts, rather than only atomic JSON writers.
Public fixtures and receipts contain only bounded lifecycle classes, counts, and opaque digests; they contain no private identity, payload, destination, path, or topology values.
blast_radius: BOT ERRORS collector and dispatcher outbox, processing, relay-processing, relayed, sent, suppressed, quarantine, test-leak, collapsed, retry, write-failure, and dead-letter lifecycles; restart reconciliation; relay retry semantics; and public operational receipts.
evidence_summary: At pinned main, normal remote claim has two os.replace calls and no directory sync, while normal remote acknowledgement has one os.replace call and no directory sync. Dispatcher claim and reclaim each rename then sync only the destination parent; accepted, suppression, test-leak, storm-collapse, and other terminal paths lack a complete two-parent post-mutation commit, and dead-letter removes the processing claim without syncing its parent. The stronger write-failure terminal helper syncs both parents, providing a positive control. Both decisive source files are unchanged from the revision cited in the issue. No open pull request touches the decisive source or test paths; merged PR #2115 addressed save-before-terminal-move ordering but not cross-directory namespace durability. Merged leaf-trust hardening improves read confinement but does not provide durable local and remote lifecycle transitions, both-parent barriers, cross-filesystem publication, or ambiguous-state reconciliation. A final path-level audit found every recorded decisive, test, and affected path disjoint from the exact 6e1672766027c16ecb06f5e122b491c0e5a0a83f to 45f4889ab5f971d920ca6a05bf857d326c42b81d delta; API and SSH main matched the latter revision, so this record is safely repinned. A final path-level audit found every recorded decisive, test, and affected path disjoint from the exact 45f4889ab5f971d920ca6a05bf857d326c42b81d to c37df83897ce9cd02829289f9f05b01347e4b0de delta; API and SSH main matched the latter revision, so this record is safely repinned. A final path-level audit found every recorded decisive, test, and affected path disjoint from the exact c37df83897ce9cd02829289f9f05b01347e4b0de to f0ece2d18883a66f04892a46669b3547e5bdf2b1 delta; API and SSH main matched the latter revision, so this record is safely repinned.
falsifier_or_remaining_gap: Run the issue-specific isolated fault-injection matrix against the exact pinned revision for every lifecycle mover, recording rename and directory-sync order plus injected rename, destination-sync, source-sync, and interruption outcomes on each supported filesystem. This read-only audit could not reproduce the temporary-queue canary or prove cross-filesystem fallback behavior.
impact: An acknowledged remote event or accepted local notification can regain an earlier claimable name, lose its terminal disposition, or produce conflicting queue censuses after sudden failure. Blind retry can amplify the ambiguous state into duplicate delivery or duplicate terminal evidence.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read the live issue identity, timestamp, body hash, labels, and exact SSH origin/main object ID immediately before mutation.
Re-enumerate every open pull request and inspect exact heads for decisive-path or ownership overlap before implementation.
Confirm issue #2427 supplies the stable identity required for reconciliation and sequence shared-helper work with issue #2464 without merging their ownership boundaries.
Run the deterministic lifecycle fault-injection matrix on supported filesystems and treat unavailable durability guarantees as explicit inconclusive results.
Verify structural mover inventory and public-safety scans cover embedded scripts and reject private identity, payload, destination, path, and topology values.

partial_findings.summary: Current dispatcher claim, reclaim, accepted, suppressed, test-leak, collapsed, retry, and dead-letter paths do not consistently commit every changed directory after the namespace mutation.
The embedded normal remote claim and acknowledgement scripts still rename lifecycle entries without directory sync calls.
Issue #2464 owns consolidation of shared BOT ERRORS Python primitives; this issue owns the transition contract and crash matrix that may consume that helper.
Issue #2427 owns stable identity across acknowledgement retries and is required before ambiguous namespace outcomes can reconcile without blind replay.
The write-failure terminal path already syncs destination and source parents, demonstrating the stronger local contract that normal-event transitions lack.

suggested_remediation: Introduce one shared lifecycle-transition primitive for collector and dispatcher that confines source and destination parents, handles same-filesystem and cross-filesystem moves, syncs every changed parent before durable success, returns an explicit unknown outcome after ambiguous mutations, reconciles by stable identity, and emits bounded body-free receipts. Route every mover through it and enforce the contract with structural and fault-injection tests.
